summary.headline: Hindustan Zinc posted record Q4 FY26 revenue of INR13,544 crores and EBITDA of INR7,747 crores (57% margin), with zinc cost of production at $903/t.
summary.overview: Hindustan Zinc delivered record quarterly and full-year results in Q4 FY26, with mined metal of 315 KT and refined metal of 282 KT, and full-year mined metal crossing 1.1 million tons. Zinc cost of production hit a post-underground-transition low of $903/t in Q4 and $959/t for FY26, both below guidance. Net cash closed at INR5,594 crores versus net debt of INR1,169 crores a year earlier. Management guided FY27 cost of production to $975–1,000/t and capex of $500–600 million, and reiterated plans for a 250 KTPA smelter at Debari and a larger 1 million ton smelter cluster in Rajasthan.

segments.name: Zinc (mined and refined)
segments.commentary: Q4 mined metal 315 KT and refined metal 282 KT, both records; FY26 mined metal 1.1 Mt and refined metal 1,048 KT. Growth came from higher ore output, better mined grades and debottlenecking at Chanderiya and Dariba.

segments.name: Silver and precious metals
segments.commentary: Precious metals contributed 45.0% of profitability. The company sold 12,000 t of lead concentrate in Q4 (about 37 t silver-equivalent including Q3 actions); Q4 concentrate sales were about INR500 crores revenue and INR330 crores EBITDA.

segments.name: Other operating income / ancillary business
segments.commentary: Other operating income rose from INR783 crores to INR1,362 crores in Q4 (per analyst). Sulfuric acid is about INR1,400 crores and scrap/residue about INR1,000 crores of FY26 cost credits; the gross-up from the third-party residue arrangement is about INR600 crores on each side (income and expense).

guidance_outlook: FY27 mined metal guidance 1,150 KTPA ±10 KT; refined metal 1,100 KTPA ±10 KT; refined silver 680 t ±10 t.
FY27 zinc cost of production excl. royalty guided at $975–1,000/t; management said it should come in below that range if conditions improve.
FY27 capex planned at $500–600 million for announced growth projects.
Hot Acid Leaching commissioning now expected in 2Q FY27; fertilizer project on track for commissioning in early 2Q FY27.
Renewable energy share expected at 30–35% in FY27, targeting 70% round-the-clock by FY28.
Silver output could reach 800+ t once the 250 KTPA smelter, LGLC circuit and tailings recycling are in place; management did not give a timeline beyond FY27.
Board announcement on the 1 million ton smelter expected around July after feasibility; conceptual plan and layout by end of Q1 FY27.
Brand, licence and strategic services fee contract with Vedanta is valid until 2030; FY26 fee about INR1,300 crores, FY27 similar at about INR1,100 crores (as stated by management).
capex_capacity: Debari 250 KTPA integrated zinc smelter: site mobilization complete, detailed engineering largely finalised; capex about $2,600/t, double-digit IRR per management.
Plan for a single-location 1 million ton smelter in Rajasthan (about 600–700 KTPA design, co-located with the 250 KTPA unit); smelter order expected in about one month and mill order by June.
Rampura Agucha tailings reprocessing plant: site work started, engineering complete.
Fertilizer plant (0.5 Mt): phosphoric acid plant expected in about three months, DAP plant around January 2027.
Renewable energy consumption 18% in FY26, with a targeted 30–35% in FY27.
Three critical mineral blocks secured (potash, tungsten, rare earths); work underway. Ore reserves 468.6 Mt with 25+ years of mine life.
demand_pricing: Q4 average zinc price $3,241/t (peak $3,487/t); lead averaged $1,931/t (peak $2,040/t). Silver has normalised from peak levels but management sees a structural deficit.

Hedging: Q1 FY27 zinc 20 KT at about $3,100/t and silver 25 t at about $57/oz; full FY27 zinc 71 KT at about $3,225/t and silver 59 t at about $60/oz. No hedges placed after Q3 FY26; policy is 10–20% of volume, within 12 months.
Q4 hedging delta versus market was INR1,100 crores; FY26 total delta INR1,500 crores.
Sulfuric acid prices are linked to the sulfur index and reset quarterly; management sees acid prices as an offset to input-cost moves.
VAP is about 24% of FY26 sales and commands only $50–60/t premium over SHG zinc, per management.
Coal: FY26 mix about 53% domestic, 18% renewable, 30% imported; Q4 domestic coal 64%. Management cited a roughly 40% price gap in favour of domestic coal.

qa_highlights.question: Hedge quantities for Q1 and full FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 hedges: zinc 20 KT at $3,100/t and silver 25 t at $57/oz. Full FY27: zinc 71 KT at $3,225/t and silver 59 t at $60/oz.

qa_highlights.question: Will silver output rise, and how does it reconcile with the FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance is 680 t, which with the 37 t MIC sale implies about 664 t already. Output could exceed 700 t if zinc falls to $2,800–3,000/t and silver stays near $60/oz, and management expects 800+ t once the new smelter and LGLC circuit are commissioned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 35% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: The third-party residue arrangement is grossed up in both other operating income and other expenses at about INR600 crores a year each; management expects this to rise to INR1,200–1,500 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 zinc cost outlook versus FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 benefited from a 7.9% mining grade versus a 7.5% FY average; Q1 grades are historically 7.3–7.4%. Management said the guidance includes a provision for input-cost inflation (diesel, propane, chemicals, explosives), with an additional gas-shortage impact of about $11/t in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the dividend plan and brand fee?
qa_highlights.answer: The Board declared a first interim FY27 dividend of INR11/share (about INR4,300 crores); FY26 total was INR10/share. Management confirmed a minimum 30% payout policy regardless of capex.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth be debt-funded and how much cash does the company hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will primarily be funded from earnings, with debt used only if cheaper than internal funds. Gross cash is about INR14,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What was the silver hedging approach and why did it stop after Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company hedged 10% of FY26 volume (20% in FY25) and stopped after Q3 because the EBITDA margin is already high and silver is a by-product. It will not hedge beyond 12 months.

risks_watch: Silver production guidance of 680 t is flat versus the FY26 run rate; the path to 700 t+ depends on zinc prices falling, which management framed as a trade-off.
Hedge book is about 10% of volume for FY27; prices above $3,225/t zinc and $60/oz silver leave the company exposed to unhedged upside, but the FY26 hedging delta was INR1,500 crores.
Input-cost inflation from diesel, propane, chemicals and explosives under the Middle East conflict; FY27 cost guidance includes a partial provision.
The 1 million ton smelter cluster has no Board approval yet; the Board decision is expected around July after feasibility. Capex and premium costs are not yet disclosed.
Renewal of mining leases expiring in 2030; management relies on first right of refusal but says a premium may be payable.
Ramp-up of the fertilizer plant (phosphoric acid in about 3 months, DAP around January 2027) and Hot Acid Leaching (commissioning 2Q FY27) have commissioning risk.
Fatal incident at Zawar mines on 25 January 2026 involving a business partner employee; corrective measures are underway.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and cash generation, with specific figures on costs, hedging and capex. Management was more cautious and vague on forward-looking pricing and the 1 million ton smelter (no numbers yet beyond a double-digit IRR), and it repeatedly deferred on sulfuric acid pricing and per-ton quantification of the other income.
